title: Machine Learning Fundamentals
tagline: Supervised learning, loss functions, generalisation, regularisation and evaluation
summary: Before neural networks come the ideas that govern all of machine learning: learning a function from examples, choosing a loss, fitting by optimisation and making sure the result generalises. This course develops them with linear and logistic regression, evaluation metrics and the bias–variance trade-off.

chapters.title: The learning problem
chapters.summary: Data, hypotheses, losses and risk; supervised, unsupervised and self-supervised learning.

chapters.title: Linear regression
chapters.summary: Least squares, the normal equations, the probabilistic view and gradient-based fitting.

chapters.title: Classification and logistic regression
chapters.summary: The logistic and softmax functions, the cross-entropy loss and multiclass classification.

chapters.title: Generalisation
chapters.summary: Training, validation and test sets, overfitting, the bias–variance trade-off and double descent.

chapters.title: Regularisation
chapters.summary: Weight decay, early stopping, data augmentation and the Bayesian view of priors.

chapters.title: Evaluation and metrics
chapters.summary: Accuracy, precision and recall, calibration, confidence intervals and comparing models fairly.

chapters.title: Features and representations
chapters.summary: Feature engineering, kernels, embeddings and the idea of learning representations.
